dish.title: Air-Fryer Honey-Mustard Pork Tenderloin
dish.description: Pork tenderloin brushed with a honey-Dijon glaze and roasted in the air fryer until browned outside and juicy at 145 F.

recipe_version.title: Air-Fryer Honey-Mustard Pork Tenderloin
recipe_version.description: Pork tenderloin brushed with a honey-Dijon glaze and roasted in the air fryer until browned outside and juicy at 145 F.

ingredients.name: pork tenderloin
ingredients.note: one whole tenderloin, silver skin trimmed. About 1 to 1.5 lb is fine; clock assumes ~1.25 lb. Pork / meat.
ingredients.preparation: trimmed of silver skin and patted dry

ingredients.name: Dijon mustard
ingredients.note: All of it in the glaze. Typical Dijon is mustard seed, water, vinegar, salt — no wheat and no soy on standard labels; confirm the bottle you buy. This package does not add soy sauce or Worcestershire.

ingredients.name: honey
ingredients.note: all of it in the glaze

ingredients.name: olive oil
ingredients.note: divided: 1 tsp brushed on the pork before the first air-fry stretch, remainder whisked into the glaze

ingredients.name: kosher salt
ingredients.note: divided: 3/4 tsp on the pork, 1/4 tsp in the glaze

ingredients.name: black pepper
ingredients.note: divided: 1/4 tsp on the pork, 1/4 tsp in the glaze

ingredients.name: smoked paprika
ingredients.note: in the glaze for light color; not a barbecue sauce

steps.title: Preheat the air fryer and make the glaze
steps.body: Set the air fryer to 400 F and let it preheat about 3 minutes. Those 3 minutes are inside the cook time. Meanwhile, whisk the Dijon mustard, honey, apple cider vinegar, minced garlic, most of the olive oil (reserve 1 tsp), 1/4 tsp of the kosher salt, 1/4 tsp of the black pepper, and the smoked paprika into a smooth honey-mustard glaze. This glaze is made here. It is not a bottled honey-mustard salad dressing and not a soy-based teriyaki. Trim silver skin from the pork tenderloin and pat it dry. Rub with the remaining 1 tsp olive oil, then season with the remaining 3/4 tsp kosher salt and 1/4 tsp black pepper.

steps.title: Air-fry the first stretch
steps.body: Place the seasoned pork tenderloin in the air-fryer basket. Air-fry at 400 F for 10 minutes. The air fryer is the primary equipment; do not move this cook to a sheet pan unless you are abandoning this package method.

steps.title: Glaze and finish
steps.body: Brush about two-thirds of the honey-mustard glaze over the pork. Air-fry 6 to 8 minutes more at 400 F, until an instant-read thermometer in the thickest center reads 145 F and the glaze looks sticky and browned in patches. If the tenderloin is thick and still under 145 F at 8 minutes, continue in 2-minute checks; extra time beyond the written window is not inside the 35-minute total. Brush with the remaining glaze in the last 2 minutes if it looks dry. kitchen_tested is false.

steps.title: Rest and slice
steps.body: Transfer the pork to a cutting board. Rest 5 minutes (inside cook time). Slice into 1/2-inch medallions. Spoon any glaze from the board over the slices. Scatter optional parsley if using. No flour dredge. No egg wash. No breadcrumbs.

recipe_version.heat: Air fryer 400 F. Preheat about 3 minutes (inside cook). First stretch 10 minutes, glazed finish 6 to 8 minutes, rest 5 minutes.
recipe_version.doneness: Center 145 F, juices not raw-pink watery. Glaze sticky and patch-browned, not burnt sugar. Rest 5 minutes before slicing. kitchen_tested is false.

allergen_notes: No major allergen tokens from the factory set (egg, milk, soy, wheat, sesame, peanut, tree_nut, shellfish, finfish) appear in the written ingredients.

Dijon mustard is not a factory allergen token. Standard Dijon typically contains no wheat and no soy; this package does not add soy sauce, Worcestershire, or wheat flour. If a specific Dijon bottle lists wheat, that bottle would add wheat — the written package assumes a wheat-free Dijon and leaves allergens empty rather than inventing wheat.
Honey is not an allergen token here. Pork/meat is a dietary_eligibility class, not an allergen token.
Empty allergens list is intentional and honest for this glaze path.

scaling_notes.1: About 5 oz trimmed tenderloin (a short piece). Glaze floor: 2 tsp Dijon, 1.5 tsp honey, 1 tsp vinegar, small garlic pinch, 1 tsp oil total. Air fryer 400 F; start checking at about 12 minutes total cook after preheat. Still 145 F center. Do not invent a second sauce.
scaling_notes.2: About 10–12 oz tenderloin. Half glaze. Same 400 F; check around 14–16 minutes glazed total depending on thickness.
scaling_notes.4: As written. ~1.25 lb whole tenderloin, 35-minute clock with 5-minute rest.

coverage_contribution: Makes air fryer the primary cook method (live catalog only advertises air_fry optionally on chipotle tofu tacos). Pork tenderloin is a different cut and clock from cider-braised shoulder and from Caribbean jerk chops. Honey-mustard glaze is not maple-mustard salmon.
near_duplicate_review: Compared with Cider-Braised Pork Shoulder: both pork, but that is a 3+ hour braise; this is a ~35-minute air-fry tenderloin. Compared with Jamaican Jerk Pork Chops (same wave): different cuisine, cut, spice system, and skillet vs air fryer. Compared with Maple-Mustard Glazed Salmon: mustard-honey adjacent wording, but salmon fillet oven/stovetop glaze vs pork air-fry — different protein and equipment. Compared with Sheet-Pan Lemon Herb Chicken: oven sheet-pan poultry, not air-fry pork. Not a flour-egg crispy cutlet redo of the chicken sandwich lesson.
